brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: Four full bases at level 1, (0..3,0,1), each holding a drained PVC-bore tray (bin:0..3,0,1~hex-bin-full-drain-pvc). They sit on four level-0 bases, (0..3,0,0).

requirements.requirement: Water pipe running through the bases
requirements.evidence: run:run-1 is a PVC pipe that enters cell (0,0,0) at its west edge (edge 3) and runs straight through (1,0,0), (2,0,0) and (3,0,0) at level 0.

Each of the four bases on the pipe has a riser (riser:0,0,0 through riser:3,0,0) that rises into the PVC-bore tray above it. The trays could only be placed after the risers went in. The configurator shows the parts fit; it doesn't show how water would flow.

Six joint bolts join the cells along both rows, and snaps join each level to the one below. check_build: ok with no rule errors, meshClash clear, and only an info note about open edges that could take caps.

finish.summary: I built a four-cell planter in a row, two levels high. A PVC pipe runs through the four bottom bases. Each bottom base has a vertical riser pipe going up into the planter tray sitting on top of it. The configurator check passed with no rule errors and the mesh check reads clear. One thing to know: the pipe and the planter trays can't share a level. Every tray I tried (full depth, half depth, drained, PVC bore) was refused at level 0 because it ran into the pipe. So the bottom row carries the pipe and the top row holds the plants. Edges that touch no other cell are left open; caps could close them.

lines.label: Bin, full depth, drained, PVC bore
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
